frequency_question: Among threatened major bilateral tariffs of this type, how often do they actually take effect on schedule without being replaced by a negotiated deal or delayed?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly threatened broad tariffs on a specific major trading partner or major economic sector where a specific deadline was set. Excludes general global multilateral tariff rounds (GATT/WTO) and broad non-specific legislative proposals.

cases.name: 2019 Threatened 5% tariff on all Mexican goods
2025/2026 proposed blanket tariff threats subsequently negotiated

coverage_note: 7 named major historical instances representing the reference class of executive tariff threats with strict deadlines.
known_gaps: Historical precedent leans heavily on executive branch leverage tactics where threats frequently serve as negotiating tools, yet major ones have occasionally been executed directly.
validity_reason: Executive trade enforcement mechanisms under Section 232 and Section 301 remain stable statutory frameworks, though institutional norms regarding tariff usage evolve slowly across decades.
